candidates.summary: Fractional-CFO 'client book': one read-only triage screen over 10-30 client bank feeds. Clients are ranked by risk (P10 runway, burn spike, low-runway alerts, unverified savings), and a Monday digest goes out per client. Priced per client, with the advisor as the buyer.
candidates.hypothesis: A fractional CFO with 15 clients has no cheap bank-native, multi-client monitor (Jirav and Fathom are GL- or export-based; most advisors run one spreadsheet per client). If Runway's existing per-company pipeline runs fast enough and its triage score reliably puts the clients in trouble at the top, one advisor brings 10-30 paying orgs. That makes acquisition per sale 10-30x a single-founder sale.
candidates.mve: Build a wrapper over generateDemoCompany that varies starting cash and payroll scale by seed, giving 30 companies. Inject a cash or revenue shock into a random 5 of them. Run analyze() and forecastCash() per company, then rank with a simple triage score. Pass if (a) all 30 analyses finish in under 2 s in total and (b) precision@5 for the shocked companies is at least 0.8, over 50 random draws. Fail if precision@5 is below 0.6, meaning the existing signals do not separate trouble from noise.
evidence: /home/user/AITX-MLOps-Hack/research_notes/Runway product go to market/competitors.md (Fathom per-company pricing; bookkeeping-as-channel inference)

candidates.summary: Consented portfolio runway watch for accelerators and VCs. Founders opt in to share only coarse signals (a runway band, default-alive yes/no, a 'raise-by' month), never transactions. The investor gets an early-warning list across the portfolio, and each founder gets Runway free on the fund's licence.
candidates.hypothesis: Investors and accelerators find out about runway trouble late, from quarterly self-reported updates. Runway's bootstrap forecast can give a lead time of 3 months or more before a P10 zero-cash crossing, with a tolerable false-alarm rate. That would make a fund-paid licence worth buying, and each fund would onboard dozens of founders at once (top-down acquisition).
candidates.mve: Generate 200 synthetic companies from seeds. In half of them, inject a deterioration at a random month (revenue drop of 20-50% or a burn ramp). Replay asOf month by month and fire an alert when P10 runway drops below 6 months. Measure the median lead time before the true cash-out month and the false-alarm rate on the unshocked half. Pass if the median lead time is at least 3 months and false alarms are at most 10%. As a desk check, confirm that the investor-visible payload can be limited to the band and booleans (a schema and RLS sketch in supabase/migrations).
evidence: note: trust risk (founders sharing bank-derived data with investors) is untested and is why risk is HIGH

candidates.summary: Post-raise 'spend creep' guardrail for the 6 months after a round. Runway detects the equity wire, freezes a baseline and turns runway into a ramp-aware figure (forward burn implied by the hiring and spend slope, not just the trailing 3-month average). It also flags when burn grows faster than plan or revenue and reports how many months of runway were consumed per calendar month.
candidates.hypothesis: Right after a raise, cash jumps and burn ramps, so trailing-3-month runway (computeSnapshot's default) overstates true runway at exactly the moment founders over-hire, a commonly cited post-raise failure. A ramp-aware estimate is materially more accurate in that window. A product that is visibly right when others are wrong earns retention through the period when spend balloons.
candidates.mve: Extend the generator with an opt-in 'raise' profile: a $3-10M equity inflow at month t, then payroll and SaaS ramping linearly or stepwise over 6 months. Run it over 100 seeds. Compare computeSnapshot runway (3-month lookback) and a slope-adjusted runway against the realised cash-out date from simulating the ramp forward. Pass if the trailing method overstates runway by at least 3 months on median during months 1-6 post-raise and the ramp-aware method cuts the error by at least 50%. Also check that the equity-wire detector (a large non-Stripe inflow) has precision of at least 0.95 against revenue and transfer negative controls.

candidates.summary: AI-native gross-margin runway: treat LLM and API token spend (OpenAI, Anthropic, GPU clouds) as COGS against Stripe revenue in the bank feed. Show token cost as a share of revenue, the month that share crosses a margin threshold, and a forecast scenario where tokens compound at their own observed rate instead of a blended burn rate. This works across bank and card rails, not only on Ramp cards.
candidates.hypothesis: For AI-native startups the fastest-growing variable cost is tokens, which run at about 23% of revenue at scaling-stage companies by one cited report, with margins eroding. A blended-burn forecast hides when token growth outpaces revenue. Separating AI spend in the forecast changes the projected runway or default-alive verdict for a meaningful share of AI-heavy profiles. That gives AI founders a reason to adopt Runway that Mercury and Ramp, each limited to their own rail, do not fully cover.
candidates.mve: Add a parameter to the generator for OpenAI and Anthropic spend growth (0-25% a month) and revenue growth (0-15% a month). Over 500 seeds, compare (a) the current blended forecastCash and projectScenario against (b) a two-stream projection where the ai_api category grows at the CMGR from aiSpendTrend. Pass if at least 20% of AI-heavy profiles (AI spend 15% or more of burn) see runway change by 2 months or more, or the default-alive verdict flip. Desk check: confirm that Anthropic and OpenAI bank descriptors resolve through the vendor catalog with zero LLM calls on noise='noisy'.

candidates.summary: Offboarding sweep for when a key employee leaves. The founder enters a name and last day (or Runway infers it when card activity stops). Runway immediately lists every recurring charge on that person's cards, plus tools they were likely the sole user of. It then drafts cancellation and transfer-ownership actions into the Inbox and verifies afterwards that the charges stopped.
candidates.hypothesis: Departures are the moment SaaS waste is created at small teams without SSO, and sub-50-person teams have no IdP-driven offboarding. The passive idle-card detector needs months of inactivity before it fires, so a departure-triggered sweep catches the same waste months earlier. That converts a churn-risk moment into a visible saved-dollars win, which drives retention, and it reuses verifySavings.
candidates.mve: Generalize the generator's Priya pattern. Over 200 seeds, pick a random cardholder to depart at a random month with 1-6 subscriptions on their card. Compare (a) the existing zombie detector's detection latency in months and dollars leaked before it fires against (b) an explicit sweep given only name and date. Measure the sweep's recall and precision for the departed person's subscriptions, ignoring tools shared by others (the existing 'someone else now pays' regression case). Pass if the sweep has recall of at least 0.95 and precision of at least 0.9 and saves at least 2 months of leakage on median.
evidence: /home/user/AITX-MLOps-Hack/research_notes/Runway product go to market/competitors.md (SSO/IdP-based tools are up-market; bank and card data is the only universal signal for small teams)
